Manufacturing Engineering Director
Electrolux Group
Springfield, TN
Job Description
Join us to create change and have an impact in homes around the world.
At Electrolux Group, our vision is to be the home appliance industry leader in consumer satisfaction by delivering outstanding lifetime experiences with solutions that always get better. We share ideas and collaborate so that together, we can develop solutions that deliver more enjoyable and sustainable living.
All About The Role
The Manufacturing Engineering Director is a results-driven manufacturing leader responsible for engineering, maintenance, and technical operations within a heavy manufacturing environment. Drives equipment reliability, productivity, quality, and operational performance through continuous improvement, preventive and predictive maintenance, process optimization, and capital project execution. Leads investments in automation, AI, and digital manufacturing technologies while managing budgets, developing high-performing teams, and supporting operational excellence and new product introductions.
What You'll Do
Lead manufacturing engineers, maintenance managers, and technicians to optimize production processes, equipment performance, and maintenance strategies.
Develop, review, and approve specifications, quotations, labor requirements, tooling, and capital equipment investments.
Participate in design reviews and approve engineering drawings, routings, specifications, and manufacturing documentation.
Oversee equipment procurement, installation, commissioning, and capital improvement projects.
Drive root cause analysis and corrective actions to resolve production, equipment, and maintenance-related issues.
Collaborate closely with production and engineering teams to implement process improvements and support operational excellence initiatives.
Ensure preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance programs are effective and sustain equipment reliability.
Develop and manage maintenance budgets while maintaining cost-effective operations.
Lead continuous improvement initiatives focused on uptime, quality, productivity, scrap reduction, and cycle time improvements.
Provide leadership, coaching, and technical guidance to engineering and maintenance teams.
Manage manufacturing-related capital (CAPEX) and operating budgets, including investment planning, business case development, cost control, resource allocation, and ROI tracking for equipment, automation, AI initiatives, digital technologies, and facility improvements.
Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, electronic, or related Engineering discipline preferred.
Minimum 7 years of manufacturing engineering and maintenance leadership experience in a heavy manufacturing environment, including leading engineering and maintenance teams.
Strong expertise in preventive, predictive, and corrective autonomous maintenance systems, equipment reliability, and operational efficiency improvement.
Hands-on experience with PLCs, controls, programming, motors, hydraulics, pneumatics, and automated manufacturing equipment.
Solid understanding of manufacturing processes, production equipment, plant layouts, tooling, and capital project management.
Experience with steel forming, roll forming, power presses, enameling cutting systems, conveyors, fixtures, and tooling.
Ability to troubleshoot complex equipment issues and perform root cause analysis to drive uptime, quality, and continuous improvement.
Proficient in reading technical drawings, blueprints, schematics, engineering documentation, and utilizing computerized maintenance systems (CMMS).
Strong project management, organizational, collaboration, and cross-functional leadership skills.
Drive labor productivity improvements through workforce planning, process optimization, performance management, and continuous improvement initiatives to achieve operational and cost-efficiency targets.
Lead the implementation and optimization of AI, automation, and digital manufacturing technologies to improve operational performance, productivity, quality, and data-driven decision-making across manufacturing operations.
Where you’ll be:
This position will be based in Springfield, TN.
Benefits highlights:
Medical, dental, vision and life insurance.
Competitive holiday and vacation time off program.
Retirement Savings Plan (401(k)) with relevant company contribution
Discounted products and an EAP upon hire and tuition reimbursement after 12 months of service.
Please be advised that we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this position at this time.
Find more on:
Electrolux Group North America: https://www.linkedin.com/company/electrolux/life/northamerica/
Electrolux Group Careers: https://career.electroluxgroup.com/global/en
As part of Electrolux Group, we will continuously invest in you and your development. There are no barriers to where your career could take you.
Electrolux Home Products, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE). Qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, disability, or veteran status. If you need assistance or an accommodation during the application process because of a disability, it is available upon request through hrsnorthamerica@electrolux.com. The company is pleased to provide such assistance, and no applicant will be penalized as a result of such a request.

Mazza Healthcare
Lincolnshire, IL
Location / Work Arrangement
This is primarily an in-office position based at Mazza Healthcare's corporate headquarters in Lincolnshire, Illinois. Regular in-person presence is expected given the leadership and cross-functional responsibilities of the role.
Company Description
Mazza Healthcare is a healthcare solutions company with strong expertise in global sourcing and private label portfolio development. We advance the cost-effectiveness and quality of healthcare products while remaining committed to patient safety. Mazza Healthcare has experienced rapid growth over the past several years and is currently seeking a Director of Quality Assurance and Regulatory Affairs.
Job Description
The Director of Quality Assurance and Regulatory Affairs (QA/RA) will play a key leadership role in the management, maintenance, and continued effectiveness of Mazza Healthcare's Quality Management System (QMS). This position is strategically important to the success of our commercialization efforts, regulatory compliance, customer relationships, and commitment to product quality and patient safety.
The Director of QA/RA will serve as a subject matter expert in quality and regulatory affairs, providing guidance to the business regarding ISO 13485, FDA requirements, regulatory compliance, and documentation supporting domestic and international product commercialization. This individual will have significant responsibility for maintaining the QMS, supporting organizational compliance, and coordinating ISO certification and surveillance audits, customer audits, and other applicable quality and regulatory activities.
Working closely with Management and departmental leaders, the Director of QA/RA will help drive continuous improvement, strengthen internal quality processes, and promote a culture of quality and accountability throughout the organization. The position requires an individual who combines strong technical QA/RA expertise with sound business judgment and the ability to develop practical, compliant solutions that support broader business objectives.
The Director of QA/RA will interact directly with customers, manufacturers, suppliers, and auditors and must be capable of clearly communicating complex quality and regulatory concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences. The successful candidate must be comfortable leading customer discussions, presenting information, and representing Mazza Healthcare professionally in external meetings.
This role is ideally suited to a highly motivated, detail-oriented self-starter who takes ownership of responsibilities, manages competing priorities, and drives initiatives through completion with limited day-to-day oversight.
Duties / Responsibilities
Support the development, implementation, maintenance, and continual improvement of Mazza Healthcare's Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring compliance with ISO 13485, applicable FDA regulations, and other regulatory requirements.
Serve as a key subject matter expert for quality and regulatory matters, providing practical guidance to Executive Management and other departments.
Support and coordinate ISO certification and surveillance audits, including preparation, execution, and corrective actions.
Coordinate Quality Department activities, including managing priorities, supporting team members, and ensuring timely completion of assigned deliverables.
Partner with Executive Management, Sales, Sourcing, and Operations to support new and existing products, customer opportunities, and domestic and international commercialization.
Represent Mazza Healthcare in customer, manufacturer, supplier, and auditor discussions, clearly communicating complex quality and regulatory concepts.
Oversee customer complaints, investigations, risk assessments, corrective and preventive actions (CAPA), and other quality-related matters through timely resolution.
Support the qualification, evaluation, and ongoing management of manufacturers and suppliers, including Quality Agreements and supplier audits as appropriate.
Evaluate regulatory and QMS requirements associated with new products, suppliers, processes, and business opportunities and ensure appropriate actions are implemented.
Ensure compliance with applicable customer, federal, state, and international quality and regulatory requirements.
Drive continuous improvement of quality processes, product specifications, documentation, and overall organizational effectiveness.
Proactively identify quality and regulatory risks, establish priorities, and independently drive initiatives and outstanding matters through completion.
Desired Qualifications
7+ years of Quality Assurance, Regulatory Affairs, and/or Quality Management System experience, including demonstrated leadership experience.
Minimum of 5 years of experience within the medical device industry.
Strong demonstrated knowledge and practical experience with ISO 13485, FDA medical device regulations, cGMP, and other applicable regulatory requirements.
Demonstrated experience managing or co-leading a medical device QMS and leading ISO certification, surveillance, customer, and/or regulatory audits.
Strong business acumen with the ability to balance quality and regulatory requirements with practical business objectives.
Proven leadership and management skills with the ability to establish priorities, develop employees, delegate effectively, and promote accountability and ownership.
Highly self-motivated, detail-oriented, and capable of independently managing multiple priorities and driving matters through completion with limited oversight.
Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills with the ability to clearly communicate complex concepts and confidently represent Mazza Healthcare with customers, manufacturers, suppliers, and auditors.
Ability to operate effectively in a dynamic, entrepreneurial environment and contribute beyond specifically defined responsibilities when necessary.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, Access, and PowerPoint.
Ability to travel domestically and internationally as needed.
Compensation & Benefits
This is a salaried position with the opportunity to earn an annual performance-based bonus. Mazza Healthcare also offers employees a comprehensive benefits package, including health insurance and a 401(k) retirement plan with a Safe Harbor employer contribution.

Head of Production
No longer accepting applications
Abstract Bio
San Francisco, CA
How to apply
Apply through the form below. It takes about 10 minutes. Along with your CV, it asks for:
a short message on why Abstract, why now and why you
one example of how you use AI at work
We read every application ourselves and reply within a week.
You will only be considered if you apply through the link below: https://abstractbio.notion.site/abstract-bio-careers
TLDR
We are building the biological inputs factory that will unlock AI for biology, starting from DNA, the first building block of every biomolecule. Demand for our first DNA product outran our capacity within months of launch, and we are now scaling 10x. As our Head of Production, you will own the factory: every order from the moment it lands to the moment it ships, and the people, processes and numbers that make that happen. You will relaunch production on a 10x larger platform, keep our quality and turnaround promises on every order, and drive our cost per base-pair down every quarter. The best candidate has run a production operation that ships biology to customers, still steps onto the floor when a run is in trouble, is AI-native, and treats every missed ship date as a root cause to find. Your role will evolve with time; you should be excited by that and step up when needed. THIS IS NOT A 9 TO 5.
Story and mission
The Bessemer process made steel cheap and set off the Second Industrial Revolution. AI is now doing the same to biological design, and cloud labs and robots are doing it to testing. That pushes the bottleneck to the build step: the physical inputs. Every protein and every RNA starts as DNA, and DNA is still expensive. With current suppliers, the DNA to test one therapeutic antibody design costs around $100 per data point; a good antibody needs thousands of them, and a good antibody model needs millions. Abstract Bio is building the factory for those inputs, starting from DNA, the first building block.
We brought a DNA product, 4-10x cheaper than incumbents, to market within 6 months of founding the company. With a team of three and word of mouth alone, demand quickly outran our capacity, so we are now building for true scale. This means a 10x larger production platform, adding long and plasmid DNA, and starting the first R&D on RNA and proteins.
Building a 10x factory is half the problem. The other half is running it every day: thousands of orders, each on time and each correct, without quality slipping as volume climbs. That is the job of the Head of Production. Our North Star is to be the biological inputs factory that gives scientists any biomolecule, on demand: the missing part of the stack that will unlock AI for biology.
Role description
We are turning DNA into a commodity, and a commodity wins on cost and reliability. For a customer, reliability means one thing: the right sequence, at the promised quality, on the promised date, every time. The Head of Production owns that promise.
You sit at the centre of the factory. Our Head of R&D decides what the factory will make next year; our Head of Automation decides how it gets made at scale; our Lab Manager keeps the lab stocked, calibrated and safe; you run the factory today. You receive methods from R&D and lines from Automation, and you are accountable for what they deliver in production: throughput, yield, first-pass success, turnaround and cost per order. When something goes wrong, you find out why and make sure it does not happen twice. When a shift is short or a batch is at risk, you are on the floor.
You are AI-native. Our factory is built so that software can read it and AI agents can act in it. Every order, plate, run and QC result lands in a structured record, and you run production on those records, not on whiteboards and memory. You use AI every day to plan capacity, triage failed orders, flag difficult sequences before they reach the line and write the reports nobody wants to write, and you build or commission the tools that do it. You report to the founders, and as we scale you will hire and lead the production team.
This is a company-defining role. We will give you the autonomy to run the factory the way you believe it should run, a budget for the people and systems to do it, and the room to grow into the operations leader of a multi-site biological inputs factory.
What you will do
Relaunch production at 10x.
Own the ramp plan, capacity model, staffing and go-live criteria.
Own the order-to-ship loop.
Every order has a status, an owner and a promised date, and you know which are at risk before the customer does.
Own the numbers.
Publish throughput, yield, first-pass success, turnaround and cost per base-pair weekly, and improve them every month.
Control the process.
Run on SOPs, QC gates and SPC; every failure gets a root cause, and the fix stays fixed.
Gatekeep new methods.
Nothing from R&D or Automation enters production without your sign-off.
Build the AI-native factory.
Run on structured data, with tools for capacity planning, failed-order triage and flagging hard sequences at intake.
Hire and lead the production team.
Build a team of shift leads, operators and QC specialists who are productive in their first week.
Be the customer's voice in the factory.
Handle escalations with data and turn every complaint into a process change.
What you will need to succeed
You have run production that ships.
You have 5+ years making biological products, 2+ of them leading the operation.
You understand the biology.

You think in throughput and cost per unit.

The Director of Quality is accountable for establishing, maintaining, and continually improving the company’s Quality Management System (QMS) and for ensuring products, processes, and suppliers consistently meet customer, contractual, regulatory, and internal requirements.
This operational leader will build a proactive quality culture that prevents defects, reduces cost of poor quality, improves on-time delivery, and protects customer confidence.

AS9100 leadership expectations include integrating the QMS into core business processes, applying risk-based thinking, and reporting QMS performance to leadership.

U.S. Citizenship is required, as only U.S. Citizens are authorized to access information under this program/ contract.

Quality Strategy and Leadership
Develop and execute a quality strategy aligned with the company’s growth plan, operational objectives, customer commitments, and risk profile.
Establish annual quality objectives, operating plans, staffing models, capital needs, and improvement roadmaps.
Serve as the senior authority for product quality, QMS effectiveness, release readiness, audit response, and regulatory/customer quality matters.
Build a culture in which quality is owned by every function—not merely inspected at the end of production.
Partner with the COO, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, and Program Management to integrate quality into SIOP, program reviews, production readiness, make/buy decisions, supplier selection, and new-product introduction.
Lead management-review processes and provide clear executive reporting on quality performance, key risks, corrective actions, and resource needs.
Quality Management System and Compliance
Own the design, maintenance, certification, and continual improvement of the QMS, including policies, procedures, work instructions, records, document control, training, and internal-audit processes.
Maintain AS9100D and/or ISO 9001 certification, as applicable; prepare the organization for registrar, customer, government, and regulatory audits.
Ensure controlled processes for nonconformance, corrective action, preventive action, root-cause analysis, change control, risk management, calibration, inspection, traceability, and record retention.
Ensure quality requirements are incorporated into operating procedures, engineering processes, work instructions, purchasing documents, and supplier flow-downs.
Oversee compliance with customer, contractual, statutory, and regulatory requirements, including export-controlled information where applicable.
Product and Process Quality
Lead quality planning from proposal through design, prototype, qualification, production launch, sustainment, and field support.
Establish robust quality gates for contract review, design transfer, first article inspection, production readiness, in-process inspection, final acceptance, and shipment release.
Ensure effective use of APQP-like planning, PFMEA, control plans, first article inspection (FAI), process validation, capability studies, and risk-based inspection plans as appropriate.
Drive containment, root-cause analysis, and permanent corrective actions for internal defects, escapes, returns, customer complaints, and field failures.
Ensure material, product, and configuration traceability requirements are met throughout the value stream.
Approve or oversee disposition of nonconforming material, including material review board (MRB) processes, use-as-is/rework decisions, and escalation of significant quality risk.

Establish quality flow-down requirements in purchase orders and supplier agreements.

Lead preparation for and response to customer audits, surveillance audits, source inspections, quality reviews, and corrective-action requests.
Communicate material quality issues promptly, factually, and constructively with customers and internal executives.
Ensure audit findings, customer complaints, and corrective actions are closed on time and validated for effectiveness.
Support major proposals, customer reviews, production readiness reviews, and new program launches by demonstrating QMS maturity and execution readiness.
Continuous Improvement and Analytics
Establish a practical quality operating system using KPIs, daily/weekly management routines, layered process audits, quality alerts, escalation paths, and recurring problem-solving reviews.
Deploy Lean, Six Sigma, 8D, A3, 5 Whys, Ishikawa, DOE, statistical process control, and mistake-proofing methods at the appropriate level of rigor.
Reduce cost of poor quality through prevention, early detection, process capability improvement, and supplier-performance improvement.
Use data to identify systemic issues across product lines, sites, programs, processes, and suppliers.
Develop team capability through coaching, certification, cross-functional problem solving, and succession planning.

Experience leading customers, registrar, government, or regulatory audits and closing audit findings.
Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional leaders and make sound risk-based decisions under schedule and delivery pressure.

Experience in a private-equity-backed, high-growth, turnaround, or acquisition-integration environment.
Master’s degree in engineering, operations, quality, or business administration.
Lean/Six Sigma Black Belt certification and demonstrated deployment of measurable improvement programs.
Experience with ERP, MES, QMS, PLM, statistical-analysis, and dashboard tools.

Commercially pragmatic while uncompromising on safety, product conformity, ethics, and regulatory compliance.
Skilled at shifting the organization from detection-based quality to prevention-based quality.
A disciplined operator who uses metrics, standard work, escalation paths, and accountability—not bureaucracy—to improve performance.
A clear communicator who can explain risk, technical detail, and corrective-action status to operators, engineers, customers, and executives.
Confident in exercising stop-work or stop-ship authority when necessary, while working collaboratively to restore compliant flow quickly.
